description_full: Flexsteel Industries, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, manufactures, distributes, imports, and markets residential furniture products in the United States. The company offers stationary and motion sofas; loveseats; chairs and sectionals; bedroom furniture; dining tables and chairs; occasional and entertainment tables; and kitchen storage. It distributes its products through its e-commerce channel and direct sales force. The company was founded in 1893 and is based in Dubuque, Iowa.

Each employee generates $40K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $4K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 4× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (4/10).
financial_summary: Flexsteel Industries, Inc. is a micro-cap consumer cyclical business with a $297M market cap on $459M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years and -1% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 8% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 22% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $48M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.56× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 1.4%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 9.8% of the shares.

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 158% over the past year excluding the latest month.

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $16.7M (6% of market cap).

growth: Revenue has compounded at 5.3% over 3 years, -0.8% over 5 years and -0.9% over 10 years, so growth is accelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 14%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.0x, 0.9% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 9, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
